The verdict

Buy the Aero 14 if…

OLED
You want the best-looking screen of the three and a machine that stays silent and cool on a train or in a café. It has the highest rating (4.6) and a strong 18-hour battery — just accept that the RAM can't be upgraded later.

Buy the Forge 16 if…

Performance
You edit video, render 3D or game. The 16-core, 55 W CPU doubles the core count of the other two, and it's the only one with 32 GB RAM, a 1 TB SSD and upgradeable parts. The trade-off: 2.1 kg, audible fans and just 9 hours of battery.

Buy the Nimbus 13 if…

Value
Budget and battery come first. At $999 it's $300 cheaper than the Aero and $900 cheaper than the Forge, yet it's the lightest (1.0 kg) and lasts the longest (22 h). Fine for study and office work — but the 256 GB SSD fills up fast.
Quick math: the Nimbus 13 costs 47% less than the Forge 16 while lasting 2.4× longer on battery — but the Forge offers 4× the storage and 2× the RAM. If your workload fits in 16 GB / 256 GB, the savings are real; if not, don't buy cheap and regret it.
